synthesis.north_star: A JARVIS for one owner: it knows the owner's world in typed, honest, labelled form; it answers at conversational speed on any surface and can be interrupted; it notices without spending tokens and stays quiet when nothing matters; it finishes whole errands inside readable grants with one tap; every value it shows carries its source and label; it knows when it is blind or broken and says so; and it grows new senses through a governed path that never widens what a third party can make it do.

ranked_moves.title: Close memory-laundering paths before the switch: consolidate owner-class and third-party episodes in separate batches, label every non-owner recalled item, and demote facts whose evidence batch cannot be proven
ranked_moves.why: Consolidation mixes owner-class and third-party episodes in one batch, so a crafted email can become an owner Profile Fact; batch membership was never persisted, so the only fail-closed repair is demotion. At the switch, untainted owner-stamped memory enters the lead's starting packet unlabelled: anything laundered before then becomes trusted owner knowledge in the target system. The critic ranked this first.
ranked_moves.payoff: An email saying 'note: owner's new bank is X / owner prefers wiring to account Y' can no longer become an owner Profile Fact through a mixed consolidation batch, and every third-party fact a butler recalls today reads 'reported by acme-billing'.
ranked_moves.outcome: Consolidation groups episodes by (tenant, butler, partition), where partition is owner-class versus everything else, and the owner partition's dedup context holds only owner-class rows. Every recalled fact that is not owner- or system-authored carries a 'reported by <source>' label in memory_context, Fleet Knowledge lines included. After the owner decides, a one-shot deterministic job marks consolidation-derived owner-class facts and rules created since mem_013 by a butler that consolidated non-owner episodes in the same lease window as content_authority='mixed', writing memory_events receipts so the change is reversible.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No new capability or tool. No change to the RFC 0038 recall contract (rank 8 owns it). Nothing is deleted: demotion is reversible from receipts, and owner Vouch (bu-jv1moa.14) is the only path back to owner authority.

ranked_moves.title: Perception spine: one typed kind registry and four stores (situation slots with the owner clock and system health, owner modes, an append-only timeline, typed standing conditions) replace public.user_context; S1 ships dark before the switch
ranked_moves.why: Situational context today is a model-writable TTL bus whose free text reaches every prompt (context_bus.py:74-93, :301, :453), and every reader fails open. Seven agents proposed about 15 tables and four kind registries for the same thing. The switch deletes the preamble with no successor (D15:753-763) while keeping RFC 0009 with 'reads are stamped' (:901), so every post-switch situation check would expose the lead.
ranked_moves.payoff: Telegram /now answers with no model: 'Home (HA+GPS, 2m) · Busy till 15:00 · Next: Dentist 15:30 · Clock: SGT · Mode: none · Can't see: house sensors since 13:10 · Not set up: sleep'. The lead says 'I can't see the house right now' instead of 'the house is quiet', the brief arrives at the observed wake, and 'what did I spend on the trip where I got sick' is one timeline.query.
ranked_moves.outcome: Four stores: situation_slots (states known|unknown|unmeasurable|unconfigured, with source, age and label; owner.place, owner.presence, owner.clock, owner.posture, body.sleep_state, system.dep.*); owner_modes (a closed git-declared set: asleep, travel, house unattended, sick, focus, hosting, holiday, emergency; tighten-only evidence rules, while loosening needs a tap); public.timeline (append-only transitions, presence edges, routine occurrences, life records and point observations); and typed owner_conditions, plus perception_suppressions. Writes come only from deterministic reducers (SECURITY DEFINER functions bound to region roles) and owner decisions. Reads go only through situation.read (now and next) and timeline.query (past), stamped with labels, so instrument-derived facts admit unexposed. Region feeders keep their store of record and publish into it: the Health record ledger, Finance and Travel life records, and the routine model (expect.* slots). owner.clock (obligations declare owner, home or utc time) replaces the 12 Asia/Singapore literals.
ranked_moves.non_goals: No coordinates reach any model. No free text in slots or the timeline. No new perception sources: the spine re-homes today's inputs. The Health record ledger and the routine model are feeders built in their own regions (vetted follow-ups).

bugs.title: 'traveling' holds routine insights and the daily digest for a whole trip: the producer re-asserts it every 15 minutes and the upsert resets set_at, so the 6-hour max-hold never elapses
bugs.why: The insight broker caps how long a context signal may hold routine delivery (traveling: 6 h) by measuring from set_at, but every re-assertion of an unchanged signal refreshes set_at. Owner impact: no routine insights and no daily digest for the length of every trip, which is when the owner most needs the brief. Meeting (2 h) holds have the same defect for long meetings.
bugs.steps:
1) Make a trip active in Travel so the travel context producer runs (roster/travel/butler.toml:116-119, cron */15) and publishes traveling.
2) Each run upserts public.user_context with ON CONFLICT ... SET set_at = EXCLUDED.set_at (src/butlers/context_bus.py:451-463), so set_at becomes now every 15 minutes.
3) The broker computes hold expiry as set_at + _CONTEXT_MAX_HOLD['traveling'] (roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:1442-1447, :1477, :1561-1562).
4) Observe: the hold never reaches 6 h, so routine insights stay held and daily_hold_mode keeps deferring the digest (broker.py:2160-2182) until the trip ends.
bugs.fix: Preserve set_at when a re-asserted value is unchanged (set_at = CASE WHEN user_context.value IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.value OR user_context.superseded_at IS NOT NULL THEN EXCLUDED.set_at ELSE user_context.set_at END), keeping expires_at refresh. Tests: re-asserting an unchanged signal keeps set_at; a trip longer than 6 h releases the broker hold; a changed value resets set_at.
bugs.ledger: Frozen-path correctness fix (allowed). Superseded at the switch by the perception spine (rank 9), whose transitions carry since-times by construction. bu-kqnum.3 note asks for the same fix-only slice.

4) Observe: a routine insight is delivered during the focus block, while the same insight is held during an ordinary meeting.
bugs.fix: Add focused to the broker's suppressing set, after dnd in precedence, with its own max hold (for example 4 h), and test that a focus block holds and then releases routine delivery. Leave the shared attention-ledger set unchanged (its other consumers must not start holding).

3) scripts/init-db.sql:151-166 creates no memory schema (managed schemas are per butler).
4) Observe: the export fails with HTTP 500 (fail-fast path documented at data_ops.py:446-448); tests/api/test_data_ops.py:311-333 mock the pool, so the suite passes.
bugs.fix: Build export scopes from the roster: each butler schema's memory tables plus the domain tables each region owns, and test against a real migrated database instead of a mocked pool. The region data lifecycle registry (vetted, arch-data-plane) is the longer-term owner of the scope list.
bugs.ledger: bu-9q1dx.14 (owner wipe) is the sibling path and must also cover the goal ledger tables (note applied).
bugs.source: arch-data-plane (scratch cross-domain.md); verified by the critic and the coordinator

bugs.title: Medication and dose records decay out of 'active' readers after about 201 days, so adherence and history undercount
bugs.why: Health writes took_dose facts with permanence 'standard', which decays at 0.008 a day; the decay sweep marks them fading about 201 days after last confirmation, and the briefing and adherence report read only validity='active'. Clinical records are a store of record, not memories to forget: an annual-checkup brief undercounts adherence.
bugs.steps:
1) Log a dose with medication_log_dose (roster/health/tools/medications.py:375-389 stores took_dose with permanence='standard').
2) 'standard' decays at 0.008/day (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:93); run_decay_sweep (storage.py:3508-3600) sets validity='fading' once confidence × exp(-0.008 × days) falls below the class's min_retrieval_confidence (0.2 by default), about 201 days for confidence 1.0.
3) Readers filter validity='active' (roster/health/tools/reports.py:214-219; src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:276-284).
4) Observe: doses older than about 201 days vanish from adherence and history.
bugs.fix: Write clinical records (doses, medications, measurements, conditions, symptoms) as permanent or under a non-decaying record retention class, with a migration that restores existing clinical rows to active and a test that the decay sweep never touches them.
bugs.ledger: The Health record ledger (folded into rank 9 as a region feeder) is the longer-term store of record.
bugs.source: feat-health-copilot (scratch health.md); the critic rated it plausible; the coordinator verified the decay rate and the readers

owner_decisions.title: Program shape: should the RFC 0038 switch carry only shape and successors, with a named second cutover (M7) for typed boundaries, decision sets, streaming and the live selector?
owner_decisions.summary: The run's slices claim the switch about 25 times, three of them L-cost. The target architecture keeps only shape and successors at the switch (label columns, lifecycle enum and tables, spine S2, minimal evaluator, packet and context.search contract, delivery rows and token, one catalog descriptor change, SLO measurement) and moves typed boundaries, decision sets, streamed replies, the live selector and self-healing to a second cutover with its own adversarial gate. Sub-questions: whether typed boundaries are unconditional in M7 or gated on a measured exposed share; whether a schema-checked ch…
owner_decisions.recommendation: (a) two cutovers, M7 scoped as a child epic of bu-4c7nvp; typed boundaries unconditional in M7, with exposure_cause as the before/after measurement; gate reports exposure by cause and approvals per week by cause.
owner_decisions.default: Status quo: the switch as written; each move's slice 2 stays unscheduled.

questions.question: Should the RFC 0038 switch carry only shape and successors (label columns, lifecycle enum and tables, spine S2, minimal evaluator, packet and context.search contract, delivery rows and sv1 token, one catalog descriptor change, SLO measurement) and a named second cutover M7 with its own adversarial gate carry typed boundaries, decision sets, streamed replies, the live surface selector and self-healing, accepting that the switch itself ships with roughly today's latency and one card per effect?
questions.options: (a) Yes: two-cutover program, M7 scoped and gated now as a child epic of bu-4c7nvp. (b) Load every harvest slice that claims the switch onto M5/M6 and accept the delay. (c) Ship the switch as written and treat all of this as incremental releases with backfills.
questions.recommendation: (a). The gate's latency criterion is non-regression and no J row moves at the switch anyway; (b) adds three L-cost items to a gate with 35 open children; (c) forces an enum migration, a label backfill and a second deletion of user_context's successor.
questions.blocks: Every move's slice 1 vs slice 2 placement; bu-4c7nvp program shape

questions.question: Should typed boundaries (target-architecture move 1 slice 2) be built unconditionally in M7, or gated on the switch's exposure_cause metric as matrix-reach proposed ('measure first')?
questions.options: (a) Unconditional in M7: the traces already show 13 of 15 leads exposed and live research never reachable for the flight case. (b) Build only if the switch's rehearsal corpus shows exposed-goal share above an owner-set threshold (for example 40%).
questions.recommendation: (a), with the exposure_cause metric kept as the M7 gate's before/after measurement rather than as a go/no-go. deep-design-1 dropped measure-first implicitly; this makes the choice explicit.
questions.blocks: target-architecture move 1 slice 2 scheduling; M7 scope

questions.question: Can a schema-checked child result with no free text keep the lead unexposed, accepting that injected content may choose values inside the schema?
questions.options: A: allow it for read, record and administer-to-owner, with value-taint matching. B: A plus reversible actuate. C: keep D6 as written.
questions.recommendation: A. It removes most approval fatigue, and actuate and non-owner messages stay gated by their own rules.

questions.question: Approve the D6 value-labelled-read direction?
questions.options: A: approve slice 1 telemetry now and decide the D6 amendment after the cutover-gate measurement; B: approve the amendment now; C: reject and keep goal-level exposure
questions.recommendation: A. Measure the taint snowball before paying for slice 2.

questions.question: Should the cutover gate report owner approvals per week by cause (rule 9, exposure-induced administer, actuation) against a pre-switch baseline?
questions.options: A: measure and report only. B: set a numeric tap ceiling as a gate criterion. C: neither.
questions.recommendation: A. Volumes are undocumented today, so a ceiling would be a guess; pair it with the peer exposure_cause metric.

owner_decisions.title: Standing rules and third-party values: may a template-pinned standing rule fire with a slot value a non-owner chose, and may third-party values reach owner-only effects without a tap?
owner_decisions.summary: The critic's injection: an exposed-but-clean lead fills an owner standing reply's typed slots (amount, date) with attacker-chosen values and it sends with no tap. Related: whether a standing rule may auto-send a message composed after reading Health, Finance or Location; whether third-party-chosen dates and amounts may flow into owner reminders and records without a tap; and whether an exposed triage goal may archive and label owner Gmail as an unapproved record effect.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Slot values must have owner, instrument or code data principals unless the rule declares the slot third-party-fillable on its creation card (critic option B); sensitive-category composition needs the rule to name the category; third-party values may reach owner-only reminders and records without a tap, while recipients, resources and safety arguments stay gated; exposed Gmail archive and label run with an undo journal and a daily digest.
owner_decisions.default: Most restrictive: no standing rule fires from an exposed invocation.

questions.question: May a template-pinned standing rule ever fire with a slot value chosen by a non-owner (for example an auto-acknowledgement that echoes a sender's date), or must every slot value's data principals be within the TCB?
questions.options: A: every slot value must be owner, instrument or code attributed (default refuse); B: a rule may declare specific slots as third-party-fillable, shown on the rule's creation card; C: keep RFC 0038 D13 as written (typed values pass regardless of who chose them).
questions.recommendation: B. A keeps the standing-reply use case (bu-jv1moa.10) from working for 'got your message, will reply after the 20th', B keeps it while closing the attacker-chosen-content path, C is the injection in finding 2.
questions.blocks: deep-design-1 move 1 and 2, bu-jv1moa.10, feat-situation-modes move 2 (sitter rule)

questions.question: Should a standing rule be barred from auto-sending a non-owner message composed by an invocation that read Health, Finance or Location, unless the rule explicitly allows that category?
questions.options: A: yes, default deny per category; B: flag on the card only, rules unchanged; C: no change
questions.recommendation: A. It costs nothing on ordinary messages and closes the silent J24 leak path.

questions.question: Within an instruction-clean invocation, may values chosen by a third party (dates, amounts, enum branches) flow into owner-only effects (owner reminders, records, owner notify) without a tap, given that identifiers in recipient, resource and safety arguments are still gated?
questions.options: A: yes, with the selector and steering-write rules. B: administer needs a tap whenever D contains anyone outside TCB. C: keep strict D6.
questions.recommendation: A. The worst case is an owner reminder at a time the attacker chose, or an attributed record. Non-owner communication, actuation of an attributed device and steering writes stay gated.

questions.question: Should owner-Gmail archive and label from an exposed goal run unapproved as record (bu-kqme7f.5 today), park, or run with an undo journal and a daily digest?
questions.options: A: record as filed; B: park when exposed; C: run, journal every exposed modify with one-tap undo, and park when the thread's sender is a security, bank or government class
questions.recommendation: C. It keeps triage autonomous while stopping an injected mail from silently burying security alerts.

owner_decisions.title: Web research under exposure: cached search for non-owner-sender sessions now, and when may exposed or third-party goals run live research?
owner_decisions.summary: Live Codex web_search keeps a provider-side open_page exfiltration channel in every session (bu-svqpzo.8 note). Options span cached search for sessions whose routed sender is not the owner until the switch, typed-slot research templates for exposed goals, and web_research for instruction-clean third-party-origin goals. The critic flagged that typed-slot templates must not pre-empt this decision.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Cached search for non-owner-sender sessions until the switch; after the switch, live research for instruction-clean leads only; typed-slot templates after a month of ledger review.

questions.question: Until the switch, should sessions whose routed sender is not the owner get cached web search (no provider-side page fetch) instead of live?
questions.options: A: cached for non-owner-triggered sessions, live for owner. B: live everywhere (the 2026-10-15 condition as implemented).
questions.recommendation: A. Search keeps working, which honours the owner's condition, and the open_page exfiltration channel closes.

questions.question: May exposed and third-party goals run live web research when the question is a catalog template whose slots accept only typed values (codes, dates, server-resolved place names) and whose provider fetches are domain-allowlisted?
questions.options: A: shipped templates only; B: shipped plus owner-authored templates (administer); C: no, keep cached-only under exposure
questions.recommendation: A first, then B after a month of ledger review. The residual leak is the typed slot values reaching the search provider, which security.md already trusts partially.

questions.question: May a third-party-origin goal whose lead stays instruction-clean hold web_research?
questions.options: A: no; D20 item e stands, and the owner's reply turns the work into an owner goal with live research. B: only catalog templates with typed slots (walk-dots). C: free-form, under a per-sender budget.
questions.recommendation: A for v1. Owner goals get live research under this design anyway, and an attacker who can trigger research spend gains nothing the owner needs. Revisit with B once ledger data shows demand.
questions.blocks: deep-design-1 move 2 slice 2 (ceiling only, not the label model)

owner_decisions.title: Owner voice: is a transcript of the owner's own non-forwarded voice note owner input, should Butlers speak back on owner channels, and may long audio be transcribed?
owner_decisions.summary: RFC 0038 D18 classes every transcript as third-party content, so every owner voice note would start an exposed goal. The amendment makes ASR an authorship-preserving transform. Also: TTS replies on the owner's own channels (local only, text always delivered) and transcription of owner-sent audio over 120 s.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Yes to owner-input transcripts (ASR backends only; forward_origin forces third-party); yes to local TTS mirror replies; yes to long owner audio.
owner_decisions.default: Every transcript is third-party content (RFC 0038 as written).

questions.question: Should the transcript of a voice note the verified owner sends on an owner channel be treated as owner input, against D18:816-817, which classes it as third-party?
questions.options: A: owner input with 'transcribed' provenance, while forwarded audio and live_listener room audio stay third-party. B: keep everything third-party, so voice goals start exposed.
questions.recommendation: A, with an amendment sentence in D18. Otherwise speaking carries less authority than typing the same words.
questions.blocks: bu-r0dsz on goals; the R27 voice use cases

questions.question: Is a transcript of your own non-forwarded Telegram voice note (or dashboard recording) your input, with the same grants as typing?
questions.options: A: owner input via the D18 amendment 'A model function whose model takes no instructions (ASR-class speech-to-text) is an authorship-preserving transform: its output carries the authorship of its input.' B: keep RFC 0038 as written (every transcript third-party, voice goals exposed).
questions.recommendation: A, restricted to ASR-class backends, with forward_origin forcing third-party.

questions.question: Should Butlers speak back on your own channels?
questions.options: A: mirror (voice in gives text plus a voice note; dashboard push-to-talk speaks). B: opt-in per message. C: never. Amendment text for v1.md:74-78: 'Voice is a transport and a delivery format. Owner audio (a Telegram voice note or audio file, or the dashboard microphone) is transcribed by a local speech-to-text service before it enters a goal as text, and a goal's final owner-bound text may be rendered verbatim by a local text-to-speech service on the owner channel it answers; neither service composes content.' Plus D18: 'Speech synthesis of goal-composed owner-bound text is a model function.'
questions.recommendation: A, with local-only STT and TTS and text always delivered too.

questions.question: Admit transcription of owner-sent audio files and voice notes over 120 s?
questions.options: A: amend v1.md:74-77 to add 'and an owner-sent audio file (Telegram), transcribed by the same connector before emitting text'; B: keep voice notes up to 120 s only
questions.recommendation: A. The faster-whisper path already exists (connectors/live_listener), and this flips J27 except clips.
questions.blocks: J27; reshaping bu-r0dsz; run 20 vetted 'long audio' item

owner_decisions.title: Household voice and room audio: defer the HA Assist household endpoint, delete the ambient live listener, and never elevate a room voice to owner?
owner_decisions.summary: arch-voice-multimodal proposes HA Assist satellites as a household endpoint under a new household origin; the critic recommends deferring it because it is the only move that creates a new non-owner audience. Also: deleting the never-deployed ambient live-listener connector, voiceprints never elevating a speaker, how HA hands over utterances, and duplex realtime voice (doctrine walls).
owner_decisions.recommendation: Defer the household endpoint until labels and disclosure lineage ship; delete the live listener (its STT client survives as modality/asr.py); voiceprints never elevate; no duplex voice.
owner_decisions.default: Status quo: RFC 0034 and epic bu-7exe4.13 stay as filed.

questions.question: Should household-origin voice (HA Assist satellites answering non-owners in the room) be un-deferred as a later cutover, given it deletes RFC 0034 and epic bu-7exe4.13?
questions.options: A: un-defer as the cutover after typed boundaries; B: keep deferred and record arch-voice's design on bu-7exe4.13 as the successor; C: drop household voice from v1 entirely.
questions.recommendation: B. The design is sound but it is the only move that creates a new non-owner audience; it should wait for the labels and disclosure lineage it builds on.

questions.question: Should the house talk: HA Assist satellites as a household endpoint where any voice is treated as a guest until you tap on Telegram?
questions.options: A: adopt after the switch with v1 'In the home, enrolled Home Assistant voice satellites are an ingress and reply endpoint: an utterance enters as household-origin text and may be answered in the room that asked from household-audience capabilities only; anything owner-private needs the owner's approval on Telegram.', D5 household origin, D4 audience field, D13 endpoint-pinned household reply rule, and an RFC 0028 delivery-not-actuation clause. B: keep in-room voice deferred (RFC 0034 stays draft).
questions.recommendation: A, as a later cutover; first decide what counts as household-audience (house state, time and weather, shared lists, transit) versus owner-private (calendar, mail, money, health, memory).

questions.question: Delete the ambient live-listener connector?
questions.options: A: delete it once satellites ship (wake-word capture only). B: keep it as an optional compose profile. C: port it to k3s.
questions.recommendation: A: it captures all room speech through fail-open gates, was never deployed on k3s, and its STT client survives as modality/asr.py.

questions.question: May a voiceprint or room presence ever elevate a room speaker to owner?
questions.options: A: never; a Telegram tap is the only step-up. B: allow as a hint that pre-fills the step-up card. C: allow as authority for reads.
questions.recommendation: A. Voiceprints are spoofable by recordings and TV, and presence does not identify the speaker.

questions.question: How should HA hand utterances to Butlers?
questions.options: A: a small custom HA conversation integration (receives satellite_id and can continue_conversation; installs code into your HA). B: Butlers runs a Wyoming conversation server added through HA's Wyoming integration (no HA code, satellite_id carriage unverified). C: sentence-trigger automations only.
questions.recommendation: A, because satellite_id is needed for room-bound replies and step-up.

questions.question: Duplex realtime voice calls (A6, J18), beyond voice notes, push-to-talk and spoken replies (arch-voice-multimodal's decisions)
questions.options: A: admit a realtime speech-to-speech session as an owner surface (needs a provider realtime API, a new D3 adapter proof, and audio that the instruction-following model reads directly). B: keep duplex calls walled; voice is ASR in and verbatim TTS out, per arch-voice-multimodal.
questions.recommendation: B. The realtime model hears audio as instructions, so the authorship-preserving ASR transform no longer applies. Duplex voice adds only J18.

owner_decisions.title: Second factor: should high-consequence owner decisions on Telegram (standing rules, Vouch, Contain, mode loosening) need a step-up from the passkey dashboard session?
owner_decisions.summary: The owner principal on Telegram is one sender id; a borrowed or taken-over phone is the owner for every standing rule and override.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Yes, in two slices: standing-rule creation and promotion first, then Vouch, Contain, mode loosening and the D4 owner-only list.
owner_decisions.default: No step-up: the Telegram sender id stays the only owner factor.

questions.question: Should high-consequence owner decisions on Telegram (standing-rule creation and promotion, Vouch, Contain, mode loosening) require a second factor from the passkey dashboard session?
questions.options: A: yes, for the D4 owner-only list plus rule creation; B: only for rule creation and promotion; C: no, the Telegram sender id is the owner.
questions.recommendation: A, in two slices (B first). It costs one extra step on rare actions and bounds a stolen phone to one-tap approvals the owner can read in the ledger.

owner_decisions.title: Goal lifecycle approvals: does one tap on a card that shows a wait envelope satisfy the settled follow-up rule, how do owner messages join running goals, and does 'Approve all' on a decision set count as per-event approval?
owner_decisions.summary: The waiting-goal design keeps the settled rule (no self-scheduled follow-up without owner approval) by showing the envelope (horizon, maximum wakes, condition kinds) on the effect's card. Also: whether waits on the owner's own answer need approval, the join rule for non-reply Telegram messages (bu-fkoexp F3 forbids proximity joins), the maximum goal horizon before an errand becomes a project, whether a replan goal may move primary-calendar events directly, and whether the waiting and plan amendments ride the switch.
owner_decisions.recommendation: One tap on an envelope card satisfies the rule; waits on the owner's own answer need no separate approval; a non-reply message joins the single running owner goal from the same chat within a short window, with a visible thread chip and /new; 'Approve all' counts as per-event approval with administer items never pre-ticked; replan moves park for approval.
owner_decisions.default: One card per effect, no waiting state, no joins (RFC 0038 as written).

questions.question: Does one tap on an effect card that shows an explicit wait envelope (horizon, maximum wakes, condition kinds) satisfy the settled rule that schedule-origin goals need approval to self-schedule follow-ups?
questions.options: (a) Yes: the envelope is approved on the card; later waits inside it need no tap, and exposed epochs cannot extend it. (b) No: every timer or evidence wait set is its own tap. (c) Envelopes only for owner-origin goals.
questions.recommendation: (a). It keeps a human approval of every follow-up's scope and cuts the refund chase from 3 taps to 1. The rule itself is not reopened.
questions.blocks: deep-design-2 move 1 slice 1 (envelope on effect cards)

questions.question: Join rule for an owner Telegram message that is not a reply: should it join the single running owner goal from the same chat within a short window? bu-fkoexp F3 forbids joining by proximity.
questions.options: (a) Join a running (not waiting) goal within 120 s, with an 'Added to: <goal> [Start separately]' receipt and /new. (b) Join only on reply_to or card buttons; every other message starts a new goal on the thread with a digest.
questions.recommendation: (a). Mid-goal corrections are the common case, and the receipt plus /new makes a misjoin cost one tap. Waiting goals still join only by exact reference.

questions.question: Does an 'Approve all' tap on a decision set count as per-event approval under owner decision 9?
questions.options: (a) Yes: each item's exact text and recipients are shown and digest-bound. (b) Only per-item ticks count; there is no 'Approve all'.
questions.recommendation: (a), with administer items never pre-ticked and standing rules never matching a whole set.

questions.question: What is the maximum goal horizon before an errand must become an Owner Project?
questions.options: (a) 45 days and at most 6 wakes per envelope. (b) 14 days. (c) No cap beyond the budget.
questions.recommendation: (a). It covers invoice and refund chases and RSVPs. Charters stay with bu-jv1moa.12 (pending bu-skbgzm).

questions.question: May a goal's follow-up wait (check back by a date, or wake on the reply) be approved on the same card as the outbound message it follows, so one tap approves both?
questions.options: A: bundle on the effect card, with the digest covering effect plus wait (one tap). B: a separate approval tap per wait. C: no goal waits; follow-ups stay new obligation goals as RFC 0038 is written.
questions.recommendation: A. It keeps the settled rule (no follow-up without owner approval) and adds zero taps for errands, which already need a per-event send approval.

questions.question: Does a goal that waits only on the owner's own answer (a decision set it showed, or a reply to its own card) need a separate approval to wait?
questions.options: A: no; it schedules nothing, and the owner decides when it resumes. B: yes; treat it as a self-scheduled follow-up.
questions.recommendation: A. Only timer and third-party-event wakes are follow-ups the system initiates.

questions.question: Should the D8/D9/D11 waiting-goal and goal-plan amendments ride the RFC 0038 switch release or a later cutover?
questions.options: A: switch release (closes the R5 regression at the switch, with plan carry into recovery). B: a later cutover (the switch ships with prompt-only follow-ups).
questions.recommendation: A for slice 1 of both moves. No goal-runtime code exists yet, so the cost now is spec edits plus two tables.

questions.question: How should an owner message bind to an existing thread?
questions.options: A: reply_to only (explicit); B: reply_to, else the most recent thread within an owner-set window (e.g. 6 h); C: always a new goal (status quo)
questions.recommendation: B, with a visible thread chip so a misbinding is one tap to split

questions.question: When the owner messages during a running goal on the same thread, should the message be delivered into the running lead (goal inbox) or should the goal be stopped and re-admitted with the new message?
questions.options: A: inbox amendment between tool calls; B: Stop and re-admit with a superseded link; C: queue until the goal settles
questions.recommendation: A, with B used automatically when the message is a stop word

questions.question: What is the default when the owner messages while a goal is running?
questions.options: A: the message joins the running goal within a 10-minute window, and /new or a reply_to another message escapes. B: always start a new goal, with /add to join.
questions.recommendation: A. It matches how people correct themselves mid-request, and joining never loosens exposure.

questions.question: Does one tap on a card that lists every exact call (recipients and content, digest-bound, with per-item untick) satisfy owner decision 9's 'per-event approval' for non-owner communication?
questions.options: A: yes, for any set whose every item is rendered in full; B: yes only for owner-only and record items, with each non-owner send still tapped individually; C: no, one tap per non-owner call (status quo)
questions.recommendation: A. Each event is still individually shown, pinned and untickable. Option C keeps the per-step fatigue that Dots reviewers rank as their top complaint.

questions.question: May a replan goal move events on your primary Google Calendar directly, or must every move park for approval?
questions.options: A: always park; B: direct moves only for owner-only blocks Butlers created (gym, focus, travel buffer), with an undo receipt, and park anything with attendees; C: direct for all owner-calendar events
questions.recommendation: B

owner_decisions.title: Situation visibility: which situation and recall data may exposed and third-party goals read, how precise is owner.place, and does the owner clock follow the phone?
owner_decisions.summary: The perception spine needs owner answers on exposure: which slots an exposed or third-party-origin goal may read ('busy till 3' vs place, body and money), whether routines are refused to exposed goals, place precision (city vs coordinates), owner clock zone switching, presence-edge retention, how the owner asserts situation (sick, away, focus), whether vitals stay fleet-discoverable or become Health-private, whether default recall includes health and finance, and the default sensitivity class for health rows.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Third-party goals see busy/free only; exposed goals cannot read location, body or routine categories; place at city level for models; the owner clock follows the phone; presence edges kept for year-over-year rhythm; owner assertions through an owner-authority capability; vitals Health-private with typed derived signals for other regions; default recall may join health and finance for owner goals.
owner_decisions.default: Most restrictive: no situation reads for exposed or third-party goals; vitals stay as today.

questions.question: How may the owner assert situation (sick, away, focus, DND)?
questions.options: A) Only deterministic owner commands (Telegram /sick, /away, dashboard toggle). B) A plus an owner_authority record capability usable by unexposed owner-origin goals ('I'm sick today'). C) Any goal, as today.
questions.recommendation: B: the capability writes situation_assertions (not slots), is flagged owner_authority so exposed invocations cannot call it (D2 pattern), and the reducer folds it in with authority=owner_asserted.
questions.blocks: Situation ledger move (slot writers, RLS design)

questions.question: Which situation slots may a third-party-origin or exposed goal read?
questions.options: A) None. B) Coarse availability only (busy_until, traveling yes/no). C) All non-sensitive slots.
questions.recommendation: B: drafting a reply needs 'busy till 3', but place, body and money stay with owner and declared obligations. Pair with the harvest's disclosure-lineage move so any card that reads a slot shows it.

questions.question: How precise may owner.place be?
questions.options: A) Owner-named place ref or 'elsewhere'. B) A plus city or country. C) Coordinates.
questions.recommendation: B: the city or country is needed for travel and time zone; coordinates stay in the connector table with no capability.

questions.question: May an exposed invocation read sensitive perception categories (location, body, routine)?
questions.options: (a) yes; the reads join label_sens and disclosure needs a card or rule naming the category; (b) refused under exposure; (c) coarse slots (busy_until, home/away) allowed, while fine place, body and routine models are refused
questions.recommendation: (c): exposed goals stay useful but cannot be steered into reading the owner's movement model

questions.question: Should the owner clock follow the phone's time zone automatically?
questions.options: (a) automatic after two consistent readings, with one-tap undo; (b) propose only, owner taps to switch
questions.recommendation: (a): it is the owner's own device, no egress depends on it, and a missed switch silently breaks quiet hours abroad

questions.question: How long are owner.place transitions (presence edges) kept in the timeline?
questions.options: (a) 120 days like routine occurrences; (b) 400 days for year-over-year rhythm; (c) indefinitely
questions.recommendation: (b): this keeps year-over-year rhythm, and raw fixes still expire per bu-s11n0s.7
questions.blocks: deep-design-3 move 1 S1 kinds registry retention

questions.question: What do third-party-origin goals see of the owner's situation?
questions.options: (a) nothing; (b) busy_until only; (c) busy_until plus home/away
questions.recommendation: (b): enough to draft 'I'm in a meeting until 3' replies, which still park for approval

questions.question: How should the owner clock switch zones on a trip?
questions.options: A: always ask with one Telegram tap; B: auto-switch on owner-device evidence (OwnTracks fixes or a landed leg), with a notice and undo, and ask when the only evidence is mail; C: never auto-switch
questions.recommendation: B

questions.question: Should routines.read be refused to exposed goals outright (a new D4 'exposure: refuse' policy), or allowed under exposure with disclosure lineage on any effect?
questions.options: A: refuse under exposure. B: allow, with lineage and per-event approval on every outbound effect.
questions.recommendation: A. A routine is a schedule of when the home is empty. An exposed goal has no legitimate need for it, and approval fatigue would leak it.
questions.blocks: feat-anticipation-routines move 1 S3 and feat-anticipation-routines move 2

questions.question: Should wearable vitals and owner measurements (BP, weight, resting HR, HRV, SpO2, sleep) stay discoverable to every butler through the memory catalog, or become Health-private and readable only through a typed Health capability?
questions.options: A: Health-private, region read via typed capability; B: keep 'normal' fleet-discoverable (today, _helpers.py:22-24); C: private except daily sleep duration and steps
questions.recommendation: A. Other regions get typed derived signals such as the observed wake state and body.strain, not raw vitals.
questions.blocks: feat-health-copilot move 1 (Health record ledger) and its security.md amendment

questions.question: Should the lead's default recall (the starting packet, and context.search without a region filter) include health and finance memory when the goal is about another domain?
questions.options: A: include, with region and sensitivity labels, relying on disclosure lineage to gate any outbound effect; B: only when the lead names the region in the query; C: never by default
questions.recommendation: A. One mind has to be able to join 'tomorrow's calendar' with 'sleep debt', and walk-dots-usecases 'Disclosure lineage' already stops those regions from leaking through communicate.

questions.question: Which sensitivity class do health kinds default to on the spine, and may obligation-origin goals see special rows?
questions.options: A) health.* = special; obligation grants ceiling personal (stubs for special). B) health.* = personal; obligation sees all. C) Per-kind owner setting.
questions.recommendation: A, with an owner per-capability override through the harvest's 'Owner policy overlay'.

owner_decisions.title: Owner law, interrupts and modes: who may break quiet hours, may tighten-only modes switch on without a tap, desk-first or mirror delivery, and should cards say which term held a call?
owner_decisions.summary: Defaults the owner-facing layers need: the D4 amendment for owner tightening, who may break quiet hours and sleep, whether inferred modes that only tighten (asleep, in flight, house unattended) switch on without a tap, closed git list vs custom modes, which proactive obligations a sick mode holds, wake-anchored brief, desk-first vs always-mirror delivery, whether travel mode activates an absence plan, whether the home sentinel may message a declared house-sitter, and whether narrowed_by shows on owner cards.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Adopt the tighten-only overlay; only owner-origin goals, sentinels and owner rules break quiet hours; tighten-only modes may switch on without a tap; closed git list; desk-first with escalation; wake-anchored brief; confirmed (not inferred) travel activates absence plans; the sentinel may message a declared sitter under a template-pinned rule; show narrowed_by with the surface privacy rule.
owner_decisions.default: Status quo: model-chosen priority, fixed-time brief, every mode change tapped.

questions.question: Adopt an RFC 0038 D4 amendment that lets the owner tighten any capability, region or effect class at runtime (deny or always ask), never grantable and never loosening catalog policy?
questions.options: A: adopt tighten-only overlay; B: keep TOML-only policy (status quo, R33 stays open); C: also allow owner loosening per capability (rejected: duplicates standing rules and weakens D13)
questions.recommendation: A

questions.question: When the owner is active at the dashboard, should proactive items go to the desk first and escalate to Telegram only if unacknowledged, or always mirror to Telegram?
questions.options: A: desk-first with a 3-minute acknowledgement deadline for alerts and decisions; answers go to the surface the owner asked on. B: always mirror to Telegram. C: owner-set per kind.
questions.recommendation: A as the default, with C available as an owner posture override later.

questions.question: Who may break quiet hours and sleep?
questions.options: A: only deterministic safety sentinels, owner break-through rules, and owner-authored obligations flagged at creation. B: A plus owner-origin goals choosing high. C: keep model-chosen priority.
questions.recommendation: A. Owner-origin goals can ask the owner to create a rule instead.
questions.blocks: Interrupt rights are derived, never requested

questions.question: May an inferred mode switch on without a tap when it only tightens (asleep, travel in flight, house unattended), or must every mode change be tapped?
questions.options: A: auto-enter tighten-only modes with a silent receipt visible in /mode; B: every entry is a tap
questions.recommendation: A. Tightening only holds noise or arms alerts, and any mode that loosens something still needs a tap.
questions.blocks: feat-situation-modes move 1 S3 (evidence proposals); feat-situation-modes move 3 S2

questions.question: Is the set of modes a closed git list, or can the owner define custom modes?
questions.options: A: closed set of 8 in git, with owner-editable parameters (duration, break-through sets, obligation verdicts) as a tighten-only overlay; B: owner-defined modes from the dashboard
questions.recommendation: A. New modes arrive by git PR, so every mode's effect profile is reviewed and lint-checked for the safety and medication pins.

questions.question: When a confirmed travel or holiday mode starts, should it activate the owner's linked absence plan (bu-s11n0s.10) automatically?
questions.options: A: yes, on owner-declared or owner-confirmed entry only; B: never, the plan is armed separately each time
questions.recommendation: A. Inferred entry never activates a plan.

questions.question: May the home sentinel message a declared house-sitter directly about a leak or smoke event?
questions.options: A: never, the owner forwards; B: a template-pinned, safety-only standing rule created on the hosting card that expires with the mode; C: per-event approval each time
questions.recommendation: B. A 02:00 leak cannot wait for a sleeping owner abroad, and the rule is owner-made, template-pinned and time-boxed under D13.

questions.question: When you are marked sick, which proactive obligations should hold by default?
questions.options: A: all non-safety proactive obligations; B: all except medication, safety, bills due within 48h and replies to people; C: none until set per obligation
questions.recommendation: B

questions.question: Should the morning brief move from fixed time to wake-anchored delivery with a bounded window?
questions.options: A) Keep fixed time. B) Wake-anchored, earliest 06:00, latest 09:30 fallback. C) Wake-anchored with no fallback.
questions.recommendation: B

questions.question: Should the grant receipt expose which narrowing term held a call (policy, posture, health, wake cause, admission state, origin) to the owner on cards and in /status, given that it reveals the owner's own mode and the system's blind spots on any surface the card reaches?
questions.options: (a) Always show narrowed_by on owner surfaces, with the selector's privacy rule hiding mode and health terms on shared-room surfaces. (b) Show narrowed_by only on the dashboard and 'held' with no reason elsewhere.
questions.recommendation: (a). An honest 'held by posture: asleep' is the receipt north star 5 asks for, and the surface privacy rule already exists for label_sens.
questions.blocks: Conflict 4 resolution (grant intersection receipt); target-architecture move 6 card rendering

owner_decisions.title: Owner latency: should RFC 0038 carry an absolute interactive-latency SLO the gate enforces, may progress drafts show on Telegram, and may Messenger keep a safety endpoint that works while butlers-control is down?
owner_decisions.summary: The gate today requires only no regression against an unrecorded baseline. Also: which seam the SLO binds and at what numbers, who chooses the owner-fast capability set, whether the lead's pre-tool words may appear as an ephemeral Telegram draft, and whether a deterministic owner-only safety.v1 egress may bypass the control plane.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Yes to an absolute SLO at the owner-felt seam (first word), drafts allowed (owner-only, inert URLs, nothing persisted but the answer), owner-fast set derived from the ledger, and safety.v1 as a deliberate second egress.
owner_decisions.default: Non-regression only; no drafts; no safety egress.

questions.question: Should RFC 0038 carry an absolute target for interactive latency that the cutover gate enforces?
questions.options: A: p50 at most 4 s and p95 at most 10 s from envelope to first reply for zero-tool owner answers, as a gate criterion. B: report latency only, with no regression against today.
questions.recommendation: A. Today's baseline is 10 to 60 s of silence (bu-z0b0ah.4), so 'no regression' locks that in.
questions.blocks: Interactive lane move; bu-juscql and bu-fd3le7 criteria

questions.question: May Messenger expose a deterministic, owner-only, template-pinned safety endpoint that works while butlers-control is down?
questions.options: A: yes, for allowlisted producers (watchdog, home sentinel) only. B: no, and all egress waits for the control plane.
questions.recommendation: A. It is the only way to tell the owner 'I am blind' during a control-plane outage.

questions.question: May the interactive lead's own words before a tool call (for example 'Checking your calendar and the house…') appear on Telegram as an ephemeral draft while it works?
questions.options: A: yes, ephemeral sendMessageDraft only, never committed, owner-origin goals only. B: no, deterministic progress only, as bu-z0b0ah.4's non-goal states. C: yes, and commit it as a separate message.
questions.recommendation: A: progress in about 2 s on hard asks at no extra model cost. It reaches only the owner with inert URLs, and nothing persists that is not the answer.
questions.blocks: arch-conversation-latency move 1 slice 2 (the narration half). bu-z0b0ah.4 scope.

questions.question: Which seam does the owner-latency SLO bind, and at what numbers?
questions.options: A: first visible sign ≤1 s p95 plus first answer word ≤2 s p50 / ≤4 s p95 for packet-answerable asks. B: full answer ≤5 s p50 only. C: no numeric SLO, non-regression only (today's gate).
questions.recommendation: A. It measures what the owner feels, and arch-conversation-latency move 2's timeline makes it checkable at the real seam.
questions.blocks: arch-conversation-latency move 2 slice 2 gate check. The harvest's 'Interactive lane' SLO value.

questions.question: Who chooses the owner-fast eager capability set?
questions.options: A: derived from ledger use on owner goals, versioned with the catalog, viewable and pinnable by the owner. B: owner-curated list only. C: a fixed list in code.
questions.recommendation: A. It tracks real use without per-goal churn that would break the prompt cache, and grants still bound it.

owner_decisions.title: Self-healing and recovery: where does the outside witness live, which heal actions may run unasked, and do failed owner asks re-run automatically?
owner_decisions.summary: The witness must alert when Butlers and its Telegram bot are dark, so it needs a home off the cluster. Also: a closed set of deterministic heal actions (restart a wedged component, redrive a sync, release a stale lease, half-open a breaker, rebuild a projection, retry a pre-transport outbox failure), automatic vs tapped re-run of failed asks, and where the encrypted off-node backup copy goes.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Witness on a second always-on owner device if one exists, otherwise a hosted dead-man service that receives only a fixed code enum; heal actions run unasked within budget; failed asks wait for a tap; off-node copy to a second owner machine.
owner_decisions.default: No witness, no heal actions; failures stay owner-diagnosed.

questions.question: Where does the outside witness live, and how does it reach you when Butlers and its Telegram bot are dark?
questions.options: A: self-hosted Healthchecks or Uptime Kuma on a second always-on owner device on the tailnet, alerting by ntfy push or email. B: hosted Healthchecks.io, receiving only fixed status codes. C: no witness (status quo: silence when the node, DB or cluster is down).
questions.recommendation: A if a second always-on device exists (full sovereignty); otherwise B, since only a fixed code enum leaves the system.
questions.blocks: arch-reliability-selfheal move 3 (semantic outside witness), slice 2, and the deadman URL in slice 1

questions.question: Where does the encrypted off-node backup copy go?
questions.options: A: an owner S3-compatible bucket (RFC 0016-style). B: restic over the tailnet to another owner machine. C: CNPG native object-store backups for the prod DB plus pg_dump for portability.
questions.recommendation: B if a second owner machine exists, since it needs no new cloud account. Use C as well if the prod CNPG cluster already has object storage configured.

questions.question: May the system run a closed set of deterministic heal actions without asking you each time: restart a wedged component, redrive a sync from its cursor, release a stale lease, half-open probe a breaker, rebuild a projection, retry a pre-transport outbox failure?
questions.options: A: yes for the whole set, with per-episode and weekly budgets and receipts. B: yes for restarts only. C: no, so every heal is a one-tap card.
questions.recommendation: A. None of these actions touches authority, credentials, data or recipients, and budget exhaustion escalates to you.

questions.question: When models come back after an outage, should your failed asks re-run automatically or wait for a tap?
questions.options: A: always wait for a tap (Run or Drop). B: auto-run asks younger than 10 minutes whose failed goal made no capability call; tap for older ones. C: never offer retry.
questions.recommendation: A. A late automatic run of a time-sensitive ask is worse than one tap.

owner_decisions.title: Proactivity: narrow RFC 0019's parking so notify-only owner watches are in scope, and who authors correlation rules and routine-anchored proposals?
owner_decisions.summary: RFC 0019 parks proactive automation; its cited vision clause does not exist (vision.md:36-57). Owner watches are notify-only. Also: who authors standing correlation rules and when a model-judged bundle class is offered as one, default watch limits, where the routine model lives given Chronicler's 'does not plan' doctrine, and whether Butlers may propose routine-anchored obligations.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Narrow RFC 0019 to effects beyond notifying the owner (and fix its citation); the owner authors rules and is offered graduations; cap 50 watches, 90-day expiry, digest by default; routines live in Chronicler as descriptions of the past; proposals cost one tap.
owner_decisions.default: RFC 0019 as written: no owner watches.

questions.question: Should RFC 0019's parking be narrowed to effects beyond notifying the owner, putting owner-authored, notify-only watches in scope?
questions.options: A: narrow it; watches whose only effect is an owner insight through the broker are in scope, everything else stays parked. B: keep it fully parked; only developer-declared watches in git. C: unpark the whole rule engine.
questions.recommendation: A. The cited vision clause does not exist (vision.md:36-57), the effect is RFC 0011's lane, and every non-notify effect stays parked. Also fix RFC 0019:44-49's citation.

questions.question: Who may author standing correlation rules, and when should a model-judged bundle class be offered as one?
questions.options: A: owner-approved runtime rules (administer, per-event card), offered after 3 useful verdicts and 0 'never' in 60 days, optionally promoted to git later. B: git-only through PR. C: no graduation; the monitor judges forever.
questions.recommendation: A. It keeps the owner as the law-giver and turns repeated useful judgments into zero-token checks.

questions.question: What are the default watch limits?
questions.options: Active cap 25, 50 or 100; expiry 30, 90 days or never; default delivery now or digest.
questions.recommendation: Cap 50, 90-day expiry with a renewal card, delivery defaulting to digest unless the owner says 'right away'.

questions.question: Where should the routine model live, given that Chronicler doctrine says it 'does not plan, schedule, nudge' (RFC 0014:20, v1.md:22-24)?
questions.options: A: amend Chronicler to publish owner-confirmed routines and next expected windows, still never notifying. B: a new 'rhythm' region that reads Chronicler. C: per-domain routines (finance, health and so on) with no shared model.
questions.recommendation: A. Routines describe lived past time, the evidence and episodes are already in Chronicler, and consumers in other regions do the anticipating.
questions.blocks: feat-anticipation-routines move 1 (Routine model), and through it moves 2-4

questions.question: May Butlers propose routine-anchored obligations ('Want a prep card before your usual Saturday shop?'), or only create them when the owner asks?
questions.options: A: propose at most one a week; the owner approves the exact card. B: only on owner request.
questions.recommendation: A. Proposal costs one tap and is how the system earns anticipation. Creation remains an administer effect under owner approval.

owner_decisions.title: Egress and isolation: widen egress only through git, admit tool-less analysis runs, and hold exposed admission when a posture sentinel fails?
owner_decisions.summary: The egress plane needs a widening rule. Also: an RFC 0038 D21 amendment for tool-less, network-less analysis programs over broker-read inputs, whether a failed or stale posture sentinel holds third-party and exposed admission, and what happens to new envelopes from a contained source.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Widening only by a reviewed manifest line; admit analysis runs as read; sentinels hold admission after two weeks alert-only; contained sources' envelopes are quarantined, not dropped.
owner_decisions.default: No egress rule beyond today's; no analysis host; sentinels alert only.

questions.question: Admit tool-less analysis runs through an RFC 0038 D21 amendment (programs with no tools, network or credentials over broker-read inputs, classed read)?
questions.options: A: admit as a read capability under the D21 text. B: keep all program execution deferred with code mode, so R22's capability half stays closed.
questions.recommendation: A. The RFC 0027 deferral rationale (nested programs escaping capability) does not apply to a program that holds none.

questions.question: When a posture sentinel fails or goes stale, does admission hold third-party and exposed goals?
questions.options: A: hold (fail closed) with one owner alert. B: alert only.
questions.recommendation: A, after two weeks of alert-only running to remove probe flakiness.

questions.question: How may outside-service egress widen?
questions.options: A: git-only profile change through a reviewed PR. B: an owner dashboard editor for hosts.
questions.recommendation: A. It keeps 'grow through a governed path' and no runtime widening exists for an injection to target.
questions.blocks: Egress plane slice 2 (arch-trust-plane move 2); run 20 owner decision 1

questions.question: What happens to new envelopes from a contained source?
questions.options: A: admitted record-only (stored, tainted, no lead). B: dropped at the connector.
questions.recommendation: A. It preserves evidence and lets release replay nothing silently.

owner_decisions.title: Memory authority: demote owner-stamped facts from unproven consolidation batches, let steering writes take their cited evidence's label, and require a save tap for procedures?
owner_decisions.summary: Consolidation batch membership was never persisted, so owner-stamped facts derived since mem_013 by butlers that also consolidated third-party episodes cannot be proven clean. Also: whether a steering write from an instruction-clean invocation takes its cited evidence's label (a security.md amendment), and whether procedures distilled from completed goals steer future plans without a save tap.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Demote (reversible from receipts, with Vouch as the way back); steering writes take cited labels with server-checked citations; procedures need one save tap.
owner_decisions.default: No demotion; laundered facts enter the switch as owner knowledge.

questions.question: Consolidation batch membership was never persisted. What should happen to owner-stamped facts and rules derived since mem_013 by butlers that also consolidated third-party episodes?
questions.options: A: demote them to 'mixed' (out of Profile Facts) and let the owner vouch them back; B: leave them as they are; C: produce a list for the owner to review one by one
questions.recommendation: A. It is the only fail-closed option, it is reversible from receipts, and it reuses run 20's Vouch.

questions.question: May a procedure distilled from an unexposed owner-origin goal steer future plans without an explicit save tap?
questions.options: A: always require the save tap; B: auto-endorse owner-origin unexposed procedures and let the owner retire them
questions.recommendation: A. Procedures steer every future plan, and a single tap on the completion card costs little.

questions.question: May a steering (owner_authority) write from an instruction-clean invocation take the label of the evidence it cites (for example, the owner's utterance), so an owner statement made after a calendar or mail read still steers?
questions.options: A: cited-evidence label plus a deterministic check for uncovered identifiers, digit runs and money. B: always the invocation's full data label; the lead must write owner statements first, or the write becomes a Vouch candidate.
questions.recommendation: A. It relies on the same honest-lead assumption as today's origin stamp (D15), but is strictly narrower. It needs a security.md amendment: 'In an instruction-clean invocation, steering memory takes the labels of its cited evidence; the server refuses citations that do not cover an attributed identifier.'

owner_decisions.title: Doctrine walls and reach scope: coding executor, free reservations, share links, read-only rendering, Spotify, PWA push, new outbound email, GitHub feed and declared sources
owner_decisions.summary: feat-doctrine-walls proposes settling soft walls with recorded rationale: no engineering executor (the owner runs a coding fleet), free reservation requests allowed (nothing charged), named shares instead of anyone-links, read-only rendering decided on measured failures, name or disable Spotify. Also: an installable PWA with web push (content-free, through Apple or Google push), sending brand-new emails as the owner, a read-only GitHub activity feed, and admitting new feeds by owner-merged source declarations (first three: GitHub, ICS, Atom/RSS; outside MCP as a read-only template kind).
owner_decisions.recommendation: Record the walls as recommended (no coding executor; free reservations yes; named shares; rendering on evidence; name Spotify); PWA push yes with a v1.md line; new outbound email after the exact-call card ships, WhatsApp off; GitHub feed only if the nightly summary is wanted; declared sources yes with GitHub, ICS and Atom/RSS first.
owner_decisions.default: Walls stay soft and unrecorded; no PWA; no declared sources.

questions.question: Coding on your own repositories (E5, B12; J2, J12): should Butlers gain an engineering executor that writes code for you?
questions.options: A: amend RFC 0038 D18 with a new bullet, 'Owner engineering executors. On an owner-origin, unexposed goal, a QA-style executor works on one git-allowlisted owner repository with a shell and a worktree, holds no credentials, and only the trusted publisher may publish its result, as a draft pull request; it never merges.' Requires bu-mc01y5 first (GH_TOKEN is still injected at dispatch.py:513-517); cost L. B: keep the wall and record the rationale in v1.md: 'Coding on the owner's repositories belongs to the owner's own engineering tooling outside Butlers; the GitHub feed stays deferred (2026-10…
questions.recommendation: B. You already run a coding-agent fleet outside Butlers, so A duplicates it, adds an executor whose input is repository content other people can write (PR comments, issues), and flips only J2 and J12. Recording the rationale turns a soft, generic wall into a cheap, settled one.

questions.question: Free reservations (G2, J40): may Butlers ask a venue for a table or slot when nothing is charged?
questions.options: A: add a clarifying sentence to security.md after line 80: 'A reservation request is a message: asking a venue to hold a table or slot through an approval-gated message is communicate; any step that accepts a fee, deposit, card hold or cancellation charge is book and stays disabled.' B: enable free `book` through provider APIs or a browser (no personal-use API exists; OpenTable's is partner-gated, so this means browser automation with your logins). C: no change.
questions.recommendation: A. It costs no code, keeps transact closed, and stops agents refusing a plain request email. B would be the riskiest shape for a partial J40.

questions.question: Publishing a page or share link (E6, J41): may Butlers create a link that anyone can open?
questions.options: A: an anyone-with-link Drive share, per-event approval on an exact card showing the file and 'public link', and a code-run revoke after 7 days (Drive cannot expire 'anyone' permissions). B: named-person share only, approval-gated with revoke (run 20 vetted follow-up 'Approval-gated Drive share to a named person'). C: neither.
questions.recommendation: B. A named share covers the personal cases (an itinerary for a friend, records for a doctor). Under RFC 0038 D4 an anyone-link is an undeterminable audience, and J41 (a quiz site) has low personal value.

questions.question: Read-only browser rendering for pages a plain fetch cannot read (B18, R20 as read-only)
questions.options: A: admit a credential-less, cookie-less headless rendering host for public pages, returning tainted text. This narrows RFC 0038:268 with 'A broker-owned render capability may load one public URL in a credential-less browser with no form input and return third-party text', and would be Butlers' first public-internet egress. B: defer until the research host (bu-6qaju2.3/.4) records how often page opens fail. C: never.
questions.recommendation: B. It flips no use case directly, and research pages already open on the provider. Decide on measured failures, not on a parity row.

questions.question: The Spotify module is enabled but not named in v1.md: name it or turn it off?
questions.options: A: add 'Spotify' to the v1.md:34-38 Modules list (one line). B: remove [modules.spotify] from roster/lifestyle/butler.toml:72.
questions.recommendation: A. The connector is already in v1 (v1.md:43) and the Lifestyle manifesto uses the tools. Classify playback and playlist tools at the switch.

questions.question: Is an installable dashboard (PWA) with web push in v1 scope, given that push travels through Apple or Google push services?
questions.options: A: yes, content-free payload (opaque id only), category-only lock screen. B: yes, with encrypted content in the payload. C: no, Telegram stays the only phone channel.
questions.recommendation: A. No content leaves the tailnet, it closes A4, and it gives a second phone channel when Telegram fails. Amend v1.md:72-73 with one line allowing an installed web app.
questions.blocks: PWA push as an owner surface

questions.question: Should Butlers send brand-new emails as the owner, and should WhatsApp or Telegram user-client sends ever go out?
questions.options: A: keep draft handoff (bu-kqme7f.6 non-goal) and keep send_enabled=false; B: allow per-event-approved owner-voice sends, never under standing rules, and add a D4 'speaks_as' field so the card says 'sent as you'; C: B for email only
questions.recommendation: C, after the exact-call card (bu-jv1moa.2) ships. WhatsApp stays off given the ban risk.
questions.blocks: J5, J36 send halves; D1, D3, B6

questions.question: Admit a read-only GitHub activity feed for the owner's repositories?
questions.options: A: amend v1.md:53 to 'A read-only GitHub activity feed for the owner's own repositories is admitted as a context feed'; B: keep deferred
questions.recommendation: B unless the owner wants the J31-style nightly coding summary on Telegram. It flips only J31.

questions.question: Should a new context feed be admitted by an owner-merged source declaration of a named template kind, instead of a line in v1.md?
questions.options: (a) v1.md names the template kinds, and roster/*/sources/ is the authoritative list, admitted by owner merge plus the shadow-to-granted owner tap. (b) Keep a v1.md line per source, with templates only lowering build cost. (c) No templates; keep bespoke feeds.
questions.recommendation: (a). Every roster change is already an owner-merged PR, and admission adds a second owner tap. It is not a plugin API: templates are internal, read-only and never distributed (v1.md:81, vision.md:52-54).
questions.blocks: Declared sources slice 3; growth loop slice 2

questions.question: Which first three sources should the template add?
questions.options: GitHub owner activity (fine-grained PAT, Events read; lifts bu-dlelt's deferral); owner-subscribed ICS calendars (school, bins, fixtures); owner-pinned Atom/RSS feeds (third-party text, always untrusted). Alternatives: an intervals.icu-type fitness API, or public transit departures (sends a location parameter out).
questions.recommendation: GitHub, ICS, Atom/RSS. All three are read-only, need no money, add little outbound disclosure, and exercise the three formats (json, ics, atom). Defer anything that sends the owner's location.

questions.question: Should bu-mzvel0's rung 3 (outside MCP) be expressed as a declaration template kind (mcp_read) under the same validator and shadow admission, limited to read capabilities at first?
questions.options: (a) Yes: mcp_read kind, read only, digest-pinned, shadow first. (b) Adopt rung 3 as bu-mzvel0 drafted it, with any effect class re-declared. (c) Keep rungs 0-2 only.
questions.recommendation: (a). It gives the 'more APIs' premise one admission path, and no outside server can obtain a write effect until a later owner decision.

owner_decisions.title: Health, routines and household data: retention, dose card cadence, strain-to-sick proposals, routine kinds, deviation alerts to others, life-record text and erasure
owner_decisions.summary: Feature-level owner choices for the vetted health and routine follow-ups: how long health records are kept, how often dose cards appear, whether the overnight strain composite may propose Sick mode, which routine kinds are mined by default, whether a missed-wake deviation may ever alert someone else, whether the life-record spine may hold any free text, and how 'forget this person' erases.
owner_decisions.recommendation: Keep health records indefinitely with owner-run erase and export; dose cards per regimen; strain may propose Sick, never enter it; default routine kinds only; no alerts to others yet; strictly typed life records; hard delete for text and identity, tombstone for numeric measures.
owner_decisions.default: Status quo: decaying memory facts; no dose cards; no deviation alerts.

questions.question: How long should health records be kept?
questions.options: A: forever until the owner erases them; B: N years, then archive; C: today's memory decay
questions.recommendation: A, with owner-run erase and export through the region lifecycle registry.

questions.question: May the overnight-strain composite propose Sick mode, or only report the facts?
questions.options: A: report facts plus an owner-tap Sick button (never auto-enter); B: facts only; C: auto-enter Sick mode as tighten-only
questions.recommendation: A. Entering Sick mode is the owner's judgment, and the composite never interprets.

questions.question: How often should dose cards appear?

rfc0038-readiness.summary:
RFC 0038 gets the trust plane right. The sandbox (D3), origin ceilings (D5), assertions (D7), the effect ledger (D12), exact approvals (D13) and fenced Stop (D14) hold up for a JARVIS on qualities 4 and 5. It is not yet enough for qualities 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7.

Nothing in the program has been built. All 35 milestone children are still open, five of them blocked, and no goal ledger, broker, runner or session host exists on main@51ec60a37.

The target has five structural problems:
- **Situational awareness and memory regress (Q1, Q5).** D15 and the core-spawner delta delete today's situational preamble and the automatic memory recall, and the lead only "may check" for them afterwards.
- **One exposure covers nearly every goal (Q3, Q7).** Exposure under D6 is monotonic, and any result from an exposed child exposes the lead. Most useful goals therefore end up exposed. That turns reminders, profile and note writes, and standing-rule promotion into approval taps or refusals.
- **The presence loop is unspecified (Q2).** There is no latency target, no way to steer a goal while it runs, conversation continuity is scoped post-v1, and D18 makes every owner voice-note transcript third-party content.
- **butlers-control is a single point of failure for all owner egress (Q6).** Every owner message goes through Switchboard deliver(), and nothing else can reach the owner when that process is down.
- **The spawner holds guarantees that have no successor.** The spend ceiling is now covered by bu-jv1moa.1 and the global session cap by bu-n92tmr, but nothing yet gives owner goals priority over background work.

There are five amendment moves. The context packet must ride the switch. The steering join rule, the latency target and the owner slot should ride the switch. Typed child returns, the API adapter and the safety egress can follow in a later cutover.

walk-dots-usecases.summary:
I traced 15 requests through the RFC 0038 target, assuming every filed bead and every run 20 move has landed: 12 personal-life Dots use cases (J1, J10, J22, J24, J29+J23, J34, J36, J37, J39, J44, J45, J48) and 3 JARVIS requests Dots cannot do (flight cancelled, sick day, who is at the door). Full traces: /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/walk-dots-usecases/traces.md.

Read-and-notify cases run with 0 taps in about 1.5-2 minutes: J1, J22, J34, J44 except the spam rescue, and J45. The trust plane holds in every trace.

The architecture breaks down in four places:
1. **Approvals are per effect.** Any goal with several effects floods the owner with one card per effect: 6-10 taps for the sick day and 6 for the flight. Once the lead ends, nothing reasons about a rejection or an edit.
2. **Live research is never reachable for the flight case.** Research output exposes the goal, an exposed goal only gets cached results, and third-party goals get no research. So the flight-cancelled case never sees live availability, and the travel planner gets one live call at most.
3. **`output_sensitivity` has no consumer.** Health- and finance-derived text can reach non-owners with no flag, including through standing rules.
4. **Monitors and archiving.** A J48-style 30-minute monitor launches 16-20 cold leads per weekday to find nothing. Archiving the owner's mail is a `record` effect, so an exposed goal can archive with no approval and no undo.

Four moves fix these, none duplicating the harvest:
- goal decision sets with a decision-woken continuation;
- disclosure lineage on outbound effects;
- typed-slot research templates that run live under exposure;
- code-evaluated wake conditions on obligations.

Taint snowballing, cold-start latency, starting context and steering are confirmed by the traces but left to the existing harvest moves.

arch-goal-execution.summary: RFC 0038 cannot finish a multi-week errand as one goal. A goal has no waiting state (D11), no plan record, and "There is no resume" (D9:624). So the only way to continue after a reply, a date or a payment is a new obligation goal: one administer tap per follow-up (settled), a starting context of prompt text only, and a fresh budget. D12's duplicate-effect protection also stops at the goal boundary. Traced on a J5-style errand (send an invoice or refund request, wait for the reply, chase, see the money arrive), the target splits it into 4-5 unrelated goals, costs 2 extra scheduling taps, and never records that the errand succeeded. The first goal completes as "email sent". No goal-runtime code exists on main yet, so the two fixes are cheap now. (1) A goal-level `waiting` state with typed wake sets: timers and third-party wakes need approval, and that approval rides on the card of the outbound effect the owner already has to tap. Each wake is a new lead epoch of the same goal, and a wake caused by third-party content runs under a narrowed grant. (2) A ledger-held typed goal plan whose steps carry code-checked success conditions. Every successor invocation resumes from it, the owner sees it as live status, and the broker, not the lead, decides completed vs partial. Both build on this run's decision sets, effect-born expectations and owner threads, and on run 20's Owner Projects, without duplicating them.

arch-world-model.summary: Today Butlers learns "the situation now" from public.user_context. That table is a 12-word vocabulary of presence-only rows. Five cron producers (every 5-15 min) write it, and they sit on top of a 300 s HA snapshot. Every reader fails open, and every session's prompt receives it as untyped text. There is no unknown state, no evidence, no per-row stamp and no change events, and any General LLM session can write it with confidence 1.0. Third-party calendar titles flow straight into it. After the RFC 0038 switch the preamble is deleted with no successor, and reading the table becomes a stamped read that exposes the goal. The target is a situation ledger: typed, text-free slots, each written by exactly one deterministic reducer and enforced by RLS. Each slot has four states (known/unknown/unmeasurable/unconfigured) bound to RFC 0029 liveness. Each carries evidence refs, observed_at, fresh_until and sensitivity, plus an append-only transition log that emits typed domain events. One trusted read capability, situation.read, serves the lead; it can be trusted because no record capability and no free text reach the store (D6 amendment). The first consumer is a model-free /now card on Telegram. A second feature proves transition-triggered obligations: observed sleep and wake replace quiet hours as sleep and let the morning brief go out on wake. A small fix-only trust slice closes today's poisoning paths before the switch.
