arch-memory-cognition.summary: Today memory reaches a session in one way: per-butler, prompt-time injection (memory_context, at most 3000 tokens, in five quota sections). It is built from the butler's own schema plus an unlabelled Fleet Knowledge slice of public.memory_catalog. The retrieval query is the whole prompt. MiniLM truncates it at 256 word pieces, and plainto_tsquery ANDs every lexeme, so the hybrid search is in practice a semantic search over only the opening words of the prompt. Recall also writes on read (reference bumps feed recency), and consolidation decides authority from evidence ids the model itself claims, inside batches that mix owner and third-party episodes. RFC 0038 deletes the injection, and the starting context packet from rfc0038-readiness covers what the lead receives by default. That leaves context.search, a single line in the RFC and in bu-u5s4w8, as the one memory interface of the single mind, with no contract for ranking, budgets, latency, conflicts or purity. Moves: (1) a typed recall plane that defines context.search and deletes memory_catalog; (2) one episode per goal, with consolidation routing each fact to its owning domain; (3) procedures, which are owner-endorsed how-tos distilled from goal plans; (4) a pre-switch fix for authority laundering, so that laundered facts do not become trusted owner recall at the switch.

arch-conversation-latency.summary: Today one owner Telegram question takes an estimated 8-35 s, and the owner sees nothing until the whole reply arrives. The time goes to two serial LLM decisions (classification, then the target session), a cold CLI spawn, 2-3 model turns, and a reply written whole as a tool argument. RFC 0038 as written keeps the cold-launch shape and makes simple asks turn-bound: D15 pull-only context, D7 deferred discovery and a trailing goal.complete give about 4 serial mid/frontier turns, about 8-23 s. Earlier agents of this run already proposed prestaged slots with a broker-only API adapter, and a runner-assembled context packet. This lens adds four moves. (1) An invocation event channel plus a streamed final-text owner reply, using Telegram's new sendMessageDraft with native stop. This also gives D10 the usage stream it already assumes but no adapter provides. (2) A content-free owner-turn timeline, so the gate's latency non-regression has a baseline. (3) A turn-minimal interactive prefix: an owner-fast eager set, parallel reads, cache breakpoint. (4) Telegram long polling. Combined target: first answer word in about 1.3-2 s for simple asks, and visible progress in about 2 s for hard ones. The per-hop budget is in /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/arch-conversation-latency/budget.md. All numbers are code-structure estimates; nothing was measured live.

arch-proactivity-engine.summary: Today Butlers has 99 roster schedules: 87 run as deterministic jobs and 12 run a model (4 of those are prompt mode only by default). It also has about 36 insight categories, each hand-written in prose across 11 producer files, plus 5 hand-coded cross-source pair detectors and 15 direct Home notifications that skip the broker. The broker already has budget, cooldown, dedup, premise recheck, useful/not_now/never verdicts and category weights. Three structural gaps remain. Correlation only happens when the digest is assembled, and only across candidates that already passed their thresholds, so weak signals are never stored. Owner verdicts throttle delivery but never reach producers or admission, so muted things still cost compute. Finance's owner alert rules write to a tool result, and three of the four types are never read at all. Target pipeline: typed, text-free observations; a deterministic correlator running declared rules; suppression by kind and subject; the bu-kqme7f.3 monitor woken only by unexplained cross-region bundles; owner watches that only notify; broker rendering from templates. Model judgments the owner rates useful graduate into declared rules. Proposed: 3 moves and 3 owner decisions, including narrowing RFC 0019 (whose vision.md citation does not exist) so it parks only effects beyond owner notification. Inventory: /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/arch-proactivity-engine/inventory.md

arch-trust-plane.summary: The K and section I rows are no closer to fixed than on 2026-10-14. Since then only adjacent fixes have landed: svqpzo.9 (bulk calendar), .11 (HA scrub), .12 (HA targets) and bu-30sah4. The runtime bypass flags (K2), session-env credentials (K3), calendar _approval_bypass (K6) and gmail.modify (K5, unowned) are all still on main. Every I row is owned, and none is fixed. Peers this run already cover the quarantined reader, typed child returns, the owner policy overlay, decision sets and typed research templates. So this lens adds the trust-plane pieces that are still missing and that let Butlers safely add reach. (1) A tool-less, network-less analysis host: R22's capability half, which today is a one-line run 20 vetted item. (2) A declared egress plane for the domain plane. In k8s that plane has no egress policy at all, and it holds every credential and parses all third-party content. (3) Lineage-carrying taint with an owner 'contain this source' action. (4) Production posture sentinels that re-prove the isolation invariants after the switch. Approval economics: exposure costs mostly capability (refused owner_authority writes, unusable non-template rules, administer parks), not communicate taps. Rule 9 already parks every non-owner send, and zero standing rules exist. Ingestion and approval volumes are undocumented, so per-week taps cannot be estimated from the repo; I give a structural model and recommend a gate metric. One live interim hole: the svqpzo.8 lockdown keeps live provider web search in third-party-triggered sessions, and a provider-side open_page call is an exfiltration channel.

arch-capability-growth.summary: Adding one outside service costs 3.2k-10.4k lines over 24-42 files and 1-8 PRs as a bespoke ingest.v1 connector, or 1.3k lines over 15 files as a context feed. The catalog has no rows yet: effect_class appears nowhere in code and bu-stbwjc is blocked. Data a feed pulls in can still be invisible to every model; for example, no MCP tool reads atmosphere readings. Doctrine already allows the first step: RFC 0018:221-225 lets an abstraction be extracted once several in-scope sources need it, and three admitted context feeds meet that bar. Three moves follow. (1) Declared sources: read-only source declarations stored as data, run by one generic runtime in the owning domain, with a generated typed store and generated D4 read capabilities. Atmosphere moves over first; GitHub activity, ICS subscriptions and pinned Atom/RSS are the first new sources. (2) Catalog admission: each catalog row records where it came from and has a lifecycle (shadow, granted, retired). A capability built from a declaration is promoted only by an owner tap backed by a gate receipt. (3) A growth loop that turns run 20's deferred gap ledger into requests matched to a template kind. Accepted requests become beads that produce only a declaration PR, and the loop checks afterwards that the gap closed. The lead never writes code, and no declaration can produce anything but a read. Scratch measurement: /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/arch-capability-growth/cost.md

arch-reliability-selfheal.summary: Today Butlers spreads its knowledge of its own health across about nine separate ledgers and debounce paths. Every alert that reaches the owner needs the cluster, the DB, dashboard-api, the Switchboard worker and Telegram all to be up. Of 16 failure modes an owner would feel, 2 page the owner reliably and 1 does so only under some conditions. Connectors that are offline or have lost OAuth, schedules that are silently skipped, DB loss, node loss, a deploy that breaks Telegram, and an owner message that fails because every model is exhausted all reach the owner as either nothing or a space-invader emoji. The one external dead-man hook pings without checking anything, sends its ping before touching the DB, and is not wired into the Helm chart. RFC 0038 makes this worse in one way: its catalog has no field for whether a capability is available, and the only health text a lead sees is a blind-spot prose layer that only the health module feeds. I propose five moves. (1) A deterministic capability self-model: each catalog capability declares what it depends on, and the broker, runner, admission and the owner's /status all read one health projection. (2) Its first consumer: when an owner ask fails, a template-pinned reply says why, with no model involved, and the ask waits for one-tap retry. (3) A semantic outside witness that sends a signed all-clear only after the owner path proves itself, watched off the cluster on a channel that does not depend on the cluster. (4) A git-declared closed set of deterministic heal actions, with restart driven by the liveness probe instead of new Kubernetes API access. (5) A measured off-node recovery point. Moves 2 and 3 build on the harvest's control-plane survivability move and go further; moves 1 and 4 do not repeat the situation ledger or the trust sentinels. The full failure-mode inventory is at /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/arch-reliability-selfheal/failure-modes.md.

arch-data-plane.summary: I tested the data plane with one question: "what did I spend on the trip where I got sick?" No code path answers it deterministically, today or after the RFC 0038 switch. Symptoms live in health.facts, trips in travel.trips (DATE only, no time zone, destination as plain text) and spend in finance.transactions (merchant as plain text). No role reads all three. Delegation is enabled on 2 of 13 butlers, and the Chronicler, which is today's de facto life timeline, projects 19 sources but no finance, travel or symptom rows. Cross-schema reads have grown to 5 view families, 5 Chronicler grant migrations and 2 schema-wide Switchboard grants. Those grants also reach switchboard.butler_secrets. Labels do not travel with rows: there are 4 sensitivity vocabularies, and projections copy text written by third parties without a taint stamp. The owner's data export is broken: it reads a `memory` schema that does not exist. The target is a source-owned, text-free, stamped life-record spine read through one typed timeline.query capability, plus stamps that follow derived rows and a per-region lifecycle registry for export, retention and erasure. Full map: /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/arch-data-plane/cross-domain.md

arch-voice-multimodal.summary: Butlers today sees images (Telegram photo/document to blob to attachment_view) but neither hears nor speaks on any deployed surface. Telegram voice notes become "[Voice message]". The live-listener ambient mic is compose-only and fails open. There is no TTS anywhere. RFC 0038 makes this worse at the switch in three ways. D18 declares every STT transcript third-party content, so an owner's own voice note would start an exposed goal. TTS is not a permitted model-function kind. D16 drops today's vision model-fit, so an image goal can land on a non-vision lead. The smallest sound architecture: (1) a D18 amendment so a transcript inherits the authorship of its audio; (2) STT and TTS as local, deterministic service-plane functions owned by connectors and Messenger delivery, never by the lead, giving voice-mirrored Telegram replies and a dashboard push-to-talk loop; (3) later, Home Assistant Assist satellites as a household endpoint with a new `household` origin, room replies from household-audience data only, Telegram step-up for anything private, and deletion of the ambient live-listener and RFC 0034's control plane; (4) pixels never reach the lead, and images become typed, labelled perception reads. Recommended amendment order: D18 authorship (no v1 change), then v1 plus D18 TTS, then household (v1, D4, D5, D13, RFC 0028). Inventory: /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/arch-voice-multimodal/inventory.md

arch-owner-surfaces.summary: Journey audit: a Telegram question and the dashboard are different conversations. Anchors are keyed per (butler, channel, external id) on the target butler, and /chat lists only the 'switchboard' butler, so a Telegram thread never appears in the chat list. Approvals, insights and notifications live in at least six separate delivery stores. None of them records attention. 'Delivered' means the provider accepted the message (RFC 0023 says so outright). The 'engaged' signal is any inbound message within 60 minutes. A decision taken on one surface leaves the card live on the others. The surface is chosen by a model-typed channel argument or a majority vote among producers, never by where the owner is. The dashboard has no live push channel: 62 files poll. Grade for JARVIS feel: one presence D, earned calm C-, thumb-first C+, keyboard-first B-. Target: one owner delivery ledger (subject, presentation, acknowledgement, with retraction across surfaces), a surface registry with a presence-aware deterministic selector, interrupt rights derived by code rather than chosen by the model, PWA push as a content-free surface, and one receipt door on every presentation. These moves are deduplicated against bu-z0b0ah.*, bu-85bqeq.*, run 20 #2/#3/#8 and this run's owner-threads and streaming moves.

feat-anticipation-routines.summary: Butlers already mines routines, but only one kind and only looking backwards. chronicler.routines records desk-occupation windows: one per weekday mask, enabled the moment they are mined, and a mined row can be disabled but never forgotten. That one kind feeds occupation inference, a daily routine_break flag and the gap interview. Meanwhile four other cadence statistics live in finance, relationship, health and core.baselines, and the scheduler is cron-only. Chronicler doctrine forbids forward use (RFC 0014:20). The data JARVIS needs to anticipate is already projected into Chronicler episodes: sleep, workout, travel and place, meals, social, music, occupation, plus owner outbound messages. The architecture move generalizes chronicler.routines into a typed, owner-confirmed routine model with window, edge and cadence shapes. It is mined deterministically, and only from owner-authored or instrument evidence, so its output is untainted. Each routine publishes a next expected window. A code-evaluated deviation state (occurred, late, missed, unmeasurable, excused) becomes a typed observation on this run's observation plane, and timing drift reuses core.baselines. Read access is owner-only and is refused under exposure. Three consumers prove it, all read, record and notify only: routine-anchored obligations ('before my usual X, prepare Y'), a Sunday week-ahead collision forecast, and a co-deviation rhythm-drift observation. Each depends on location, home, spend and wearable data that Dots does not have. The model needs one Chronicler doctrine amendment and one D4 exposure amendment, and it names its retention, forget and kind opt-in controls.

feat-situation-modes.summary: Butlers has no first-class owner mode. Twelve RFC 0009 context signals stand in for one. RFC 0009 says consumers opt in and each decides for itself (RFC 0009:474-485; architecture.md:408-411). The result: 7 of the 12 signals (sick, away, focused, exercising, socializing, commuting, in_space) change nothing deterministic and reach only the model's prompt preamble. The two gates that do read situation use different signal sets. The scheduler reads no situation at all. The owner cannot see or change the current state from any surface. Two behaviour bugs: a refresh defect lets 'traveling' hold routine insights and the daily digest for an entire trip, and 'focus' blocks suppress nothing while ordinary meetings do. This run's harvest already designed the parts: situation ledger, observed sleep, owner clock, obligation guards, derived interrupt rights and policy overlay. Run 16 added the break-through list, absence plans and the disruption window. No one owns the composition: a typed mode the owner can see, with entry evidence, expiry, a fold rule and one effect profile that every gate reads. Move 1 is that architecture; it rides the RFC 0038 switch with the situation ledger. Move 2 is the first mode that loosens something, with the confirmation rule that requires: 'house attended' (sitter or cleaner) separated from 'owner away' for the home sentinel. Move 3 is a cheap, owner-written entry signal: the Gmail vacation responder, readable under the already-granted gmail.readonly scope. The full inventory is in /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/feat-situation-modes/modes.md. I did not propose the sick-day fallout card, travel local time or wake-anchored release: the run 16 disruption window and this run's premise replan, owner clock and observed-sleep moves already cover them.

feat-health-copilot.summary: Health is where Butlers clearly leads Dots (matrix row B24: Dots has no wearable, medication or symptom data), but the substrate isn't yet a trustworthy health record. Three problems stand out. First, every clinical row (vitals, doses, symptoms, medications) is stored as a decaying memory fact. Wearable vitals go 'fading' after about 201 days and 'expired' after about 374 days, so readers that filter on validity='active' lose them. Second, wearable vitals are deliberately tagged sensitivity 'normal', which puts them in the fleet-shared memory catalog. Third, wellness envelopes still reach Health as a routed request whose prompt tells the session to call one tool. On the feature side: no reminder fires when a dose is due. The 06:55 briefing marks every active medication 'missed today', whatever its frequency. Baselines cover only resting HR, HRV and sleep duration, each judged alone. Four moves follow. (1) A health record ledger: a typed, non-decaying, Health-private store fed by a deterministic service-plane writer. This is the architecture move, and its first consumer is the visit brief. (2) A regimen and dose loop. (3) An overnight-strain composite that proposes Sick mode. (4) Closing the loop after appointments. Moves 2-4 build by name on this run's owner modes, observation plane, observed sleep/wake and effect-born expectations; none of them restates those moves. Inventory is in /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/feat-health-copilot/health.md.

deep-design-1.summary:
This design replaces the single goal-wide exposure bit in RFC 0038 D6 with a label on every invocation, tracked separately per invocation. A label has three parts. I (instruction principals) is everyone who could have written instructions into the context. D (data principals) is everyone who chose values the context holds. C is the set of sensitivity categories. Each label also points to the goal and invocation that wrote it. Labels join by union. An invocation is exposed only when I contains someone outside TCB, where TCB is the owner, instruments and code. This per-invocation tracking is sound because D3:261-266 already gives every invocation its own kernel domain, so the only channels between invocations go through the broker, and the broker can label each one.

Free text reaches a model in two ways. As raw free text, it adds its author to I and D. As an opaque handle, it adds nothing until the handle is read. A typed boundary turns I into D. Typed boundaries are deterministic code, a schema-checked quarantined extraction, a schema-checked child return and a schema-checked research return. Their output uses a closed type set that has no strings, names, hostnames or URLs.

Two call-time rules close the remaining channel, which is values an attacker chooses:
- **Selector rule.** A recipient, resource or safety argument whose identifier the broker delivered only under a third-party D (or cannot attribute) is gated as exposed for that call.
- **Steering-write rule.** A steering write must come from an invocation whose I is in TCB. The write takes the label of the evidence it cites. The broker refuses a write that contains an attributed identifier, account-like number or money value its citations do not cover.

What this merges, drops and keeps:
- **Merged:** typed child returns and value-labelled reads become one typed-boundary mechanism. The stamps that travel with rows, the recall labels, taint_goal_id and taint_sources, the disclosure_set and the four sensitivity vocabularies all become fields of the one label.
- **Dropped:** typed-slot research templates as an exposure fix. They remain only as an open question about the third-party ceiling. Also dropped: value-taint matching on scalar values.
- **Kept:** authorship-carrying ASR as a label-preserving transform; perception reads and situation reducers as typed boundaries; Vouch (bu-jv1moa.14) as owner declassification of integrity; owner card approval and C-naming standing rules as declassification of sensitivity.

Measured against the traces: exposed leads drop from 13 of 15 to 0. Live research returns in 4 traces. Live links return in 4 notifies. Taps barely move: 0 of about 27 in walk-dots and 3 in days.md, because almost every remaining tap is owner rule 9 or tool approval policy, by design.

Releases. Move 1, the label data model and per-invocation accounting, must ride the RFC 0038 switch: the taint, ledger and catalog columns are being built now (bu-pkuny2, bu-fkoexp, bu-stbwjc), and a boolean shipped today means a backfill later. Move 2, the typed boundaries, rides a later label-precision cutover with its own adversarial gate.

deep-design-2.summary:
This design gives the RFC 0038 goal one lifecycle. It merges the waiting goals, plan ledger, decision sets, owner threads and inbox, steering, effect-born expectations, the wake packet and wake conditions that earlier agents proposed separately. It builds on deep-design-1's labels and does not redesign taint.

State machine (goal):
- States: admitted -> running -> waiting -> running ... -> completed | partial | failed | stopped | budget_exhausted.
- awaiting_approval, settling and recovering are deleted. Waiting holds no session.
- Recovery, relaunch, escalation and wake each advance lead_epoch (one counter).

Who causes each transition:
- The runner launches epoch 1.
- The lead calls goal.wait or goal.propose, or ends with parked effects, and the broker moves the goal to waiting.
- A typed condition fires and the runner launches epoch+1. The causes are: an owner decision or owner input (owner); expectation(id) (connector evidence); at(t) (timer); effect_settled (domain receipt).
- The broker closes a goal without any lead when the fired condition settles every remaining plan step (completed), or when the deadline passes (partial).
- Only the owner can Stop.

Records (Switchboard goal ledger, beside sw_047 in draft PR #4574):
- owner_threads and thread_bindings.
- goal_inbox, which absorbs bu-fkoexp F3 'joined' (that join has no delivery path today).
- goal_plan_versions.
- goal_wait_envelopes: owner-approved horizon, maximum wakes and allowed kinds.
- goal_waits: at most one open per goal.
- goal_wakes: receipts.
- decision_sets.
- Expectations stay in the RFC 0026 condition ledger.

Grant for each epoch = goal ceiling ∩ wake-cause ceiling. When the cause is evidence written by a principal outside the TCB, the epoch gets the D5 third_party ceiling. A wake is treated as a caused admission into the same goal.

The settled self-scheduling rule is kept with fewer taps. A timer or evidence wait needs an owner-approved envelope, approved on the card of the effect that motivates it. Owner-decision, owner-input and settlement waits need none. An exposed epoch can wait only inside an existing envelope.

Traced errands:

| Errand | Before (goals, taps) | After (goals, taps) | Other change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-week Acme refund chase | 6, 3 | 1, 1 | 2 lead epochs plus 1 broker-closed completion |
| Sick-day replan | 2, 3 | 1, 2 | |
| Plumber correction | 2, 4 | 1, 1 | |

Releases:
- Slice 1 must ride the RFC 0038 switch: states, waits and envelopes, inbox and join rule, the plan carry, and the wake packet. The ledger enum is being written now in PR #4574, and the switch otherwise ships the R5 regression and approval waits that hold sandbox slots.
- Decision sets, broker-computed completion and expectation wakes ride the first cutover after the switch.

deep-design-3.summary: This merges the seven perception proposals into one spine. One git kind registry uses deep-design-1's closed type set and feeds four stores: situation_slots (current state, including owner.clock, the owner.posture derived from modes, system.dep instrument health and the next windows of confirmed expectations), owner_modes (the only store the owner writes), an append-only public.timeline (transitions, presence edges, routine occurrences, projected life records) and a typed owner_conditions (standing observations). One suppressions table sits beside them. The lead gets two stamped read capabilities: situation.read for now and next, and timeline.query for the past. Capability health is computed when it is read and has no table, and the owner clock is a slot rather than a table. About 15 proposed new tables shrink to 4 stores plus 1 suppression table, with an owner-place registry and a mirror of the kinds registry kept as configuration. The design flips arch-world-model's 'trusted' read to stamped-with-labels to obey RFC 0038 D4. It needs D6/D5 amendments so instrument-derived transitions admit unexposed. RFC 0029's absent state is treated as evidence for the reducer, not as 'unknown'. Two moves: the spine itself, and its first consumers (/now card and departure edge before the switch, observed sleep with a wake-anchored brief at the switch).

critic.summary: Novelty attack on 22 moves across 22 harvest keys: 10 novel, 11 partly filed (closest beads named), 1 effectively a duplicate (arch-reliability 'Measured recovery point' = bu-10bbqg + bu-kqnum.8 + bu-e1410). Nothing spends, books or touches Slack; nothing gives the lead web or shell; no move reopens the schedule-origin rule. Direction flags: walk-dots 'typed-slot research templates' pre-empts the still-open bu-svqpzo.8 owner decision and widens the D20 third-party ceiling (deep-design-1 already drops it); arch-voice 'household endpoint' is a non-owner reply surface that needs the v1/D5/D13 amendments it declares and should be scored as a later cutover, not the switch; deep-design-2's 'settlement waits need no envelope' must be stated as inside an already-approved effect or it quietly weakens the settled follow-up rule. Hard look at deep-design-1: the selector and steering-write rules gate recipient, resource and safety identifiers, but RFC 0038 D13 (:718-722) lets a template-pinned standing rule take 'dates, amounts, identifiers' as slot values, and neither D13 nor the design's D13 amendment checks the data principals of those values, so an attacker email typed as {amount, date, existing payee id} can fire an owner-made standing reply to a pinned recipient with attacker-chosen content and no tap, from a clean lead. Claim checks: Telegram sendMessageDraft exists (Bot API 9.3, 2025-12-31; can_stop/keep_on_stop and MessageGenerationStopped in 10.3, 2026-08-24); no goal ledger, broker, runner or session host exists on main@51ec60a37 (rg over src/ roster/ migrations/ for goal_runtime|effect_class|session_host|authorization_broker: 0 files). All three candidate bugs are real; the briefing one is worse than claimed (it runs at 06:55 over the whole SGT day, so every medication not dosed before 06:55 is 'Missed dose(s) today') and sits in src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:268-302, not roster/health/jobs/. Three further claims confirmed: 12 Asia/Singapore literals in src/ and roster/ .py (walk-jarvis-day said four), the Helm chart has no egress NetworkPolicy for domain pods (only host-ingress and tracker-egress), and the external dead-man pings before touching the DB and is wired only in docker-compose, not Helm. Missing lenses: owner-principal strength (Telegram sender id is the only owner factor; doctrine never defines 'verified owner'), cost economics of a 5-session JARVIS, a rehearsal corpus for qualities 1-3, and third-person privacy beyond erasure. Top-15 ranking in measurements.

target-architecture.summary: RFC 0038 builds the trust plane (D3 sandbox, D4 catalog, D5 ceilings, D7 assertions, D12 ledger, D13 exact approvals, D14 Stop) and carries qualities 4 and 5 most of the way, but it gives the mind no world (Q1 regresses when D15 deletes the preamble with no successor), no conversation that lasts (D9 no resume, D11 awaiting_approval holds a sandbox slot), no way to notice without spending tokens (Q3), no self (D4 has no availability field) and no governed growth path, and its goal-wide exposure bit leaves 13 of 15 traced leads exposed. The smallest coherent set is six program-level moves on four planes: a label plane (per-invocation labels, typed boundaries) replacing D6's boolean; a perception spine (typed slots, owner modes, append-only timeline, typed conditions) replacing public.user_context; one goal lifecycle (waiting, envelopes, thread and inbox, plan, decision sets, evidence-closed completion); one condition evaluator shared by waits, plan steps, obligations, watches, correlation rules, modes and expectations (today four proposals each invent a predicate language and nobody owns the evaluator); a starting context packet and context.search contract that gives D15 a successor; and an owner loop (interactive lane, streamed reply, delivery ledger, surface selector, derived interrupt rights). Self-model, healing, egress, growth and modality services follow on these contracts. About 25 harvest slices claim the switch, including three L-cost items; the switch should carry only shape and successors (label columns, lifecycle enum and tables, spine S2 and user_context deletion, minimal evaluator, packet and recall contract, delivery rows and one sv1 token, one catalog descriptor change), and a named second cutover (M7, own adversarial gate) carries typed boundaries, decision sets, streaming, the live selector and self-healing. Spine S1 must ship dark before the switch because the frame, posture gate and owner clock need it. Ten unresolved conflicts are settled, among them: thread vs delivery subject vs decision set (three records, one token family), the context packet reading user_context that the spine deletes, six grant-narrowing inputs with no order or receipt, three surviving sensitivity vocabularies, and draft PR #4574 baking in awaiting_approval/settling/recovering, boolean exposure and an immutability trigger that blocks thread_id, labels and plan carry. Full layered architecture, dependency graph, release plan, conflicts and scorecard: /home/orca/orca/projects/butlers/.tmp/jarvis-arch-pursuit-2026-10-16/scratch/target-architecture/target.md.
